smt-2022-algebra-tiebreaker-01.title: Cauchy-Schwarz
smt-2022-algebra-tiebreaker-01.body:
Write $x+2y+3z=1\cdot x+\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt2y+\sqrt3\cdot\sqrt3z$. By Cauchy-Schwarz, $(x+2y+3z)^2\le(1+2+3)(x^2+2y^2+3z^2)=6\cdot96=576$, so $x+2y+3z\le24$.

Equality holds when $x=y=z$ (proportional to $(1,\sqrt2,\sqrt3)$ after scaling): $x=y=z=4$ gives $16+32+48=96$ and $4+8+12=24$.

**Answer: 24**

smt-2022-algebra-tiebreaker-02.title: Describe the first region
smt-2022-algebra-tiebreaker-02.body:
$\left|\frac1z-1\right|<1\iff|1-z|<|z|$ (for $z\ne0$), i.e. $z$ is closer to $1$ than to $0$, i.e. $\operatorname{Re}z>\frac12$.

The second condition is the open disc of radius $1$ centred at $1$. So we need the part of that disc to the right of the line $x=\frac12$.

The line is at distance $\frac12$ from the centre, so it cuts a chord subtending $120^\circ$ (since $\cos\frac\theta2=\frac12$ gives $\theta=120^\circ$). The region on the far side from the cut is the whole disc minus a $120^\circ$ circular segment on the left, i.e. a $240^\circ$ sector ($\frac23$ of the disc) plus the triangle formed by the centre and the chord.

Area $=\frac23\pi+\frac12\cdot1\cdot1\cdot\sin120^\circ=\frac{2\pi}3+\frac{\sqrt3}4$.

**Answer: $\frac{2\pi}{3}+\frac{\sqrt3}4$**

smt-2022-algebra-tiebreaker-03.title: Telescoping bounds
smt-2022-algebra-tiebreaker-03.body:
Let $P$ be the product. Since $\frac{2n+3}{2n+2}<\frac{2n+2}{2n+1}$, we have $\left(\frac{2n+2}{2n+1}\right)^2>\frac{2n+2}{2n+1}\cdot\frac{2n+3}{2n+2}=\frac{2n+3}{2n+1}$, and the product of these telescopes: $P^2>\frac{4047}{5}=809.4>784$, so $P>28$.

For an upper bound, peel off the first two factors: $P=\frac65\cdot\frac87\cdot P''$ with $P''=\prod_{n=4}^{2022}\frac{2n+2}{2n+1}$. Since $\frac{2n+2}{2n+1}<\frac{2n+1}{2n}$, $P''^2<\prod_{n=4}^{2022}\frac{2n+2}{2n+1}\cdot\frac{2n+1}{2n}=\prod_{n=4}^{2022}\frac{n+1}{n}=\frac{2023}{4}$. Hence $P^2<\frac{36}{25}\cdot\frac{64}{49}\cdot\frac{2023}4\approx951.3<961$, so $P<31$.

So $28<P<31$; the floor is $28$, $29$ or $30$. It is stated to be coprime to $2022=2\cdot3\cdot337$, which rules out $28$ and $30$ (both even). Hence the answer is $29$. (Direct computation gives $P\approx29.90$.)

**Answer: 29**
